card_limitations: Canonical repository moved to opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.
Server0.2.3 and Python SDK0.1.16 are separate; help/import is not isolation proof.
Container sandbox strength depends on configured runtime and host isolation.
candidates.name: opensandbox
candidates.role: Self-hostable sandbox control API and SDKs

card_limitations: Native proof covers local health, provisioned data sources/dashboard queries and the receipt-specific UI checks; no external dashboard publication or high availability.
AGPL-3.0-only applies with documented component exceptions; hosted-service terms are separate.
A successful dashboard query does not validate profitable strategy performance or maximum token efficiency.
candidates.name: Grafana

card_limitations: Filesystem allowed/denied operations were proven; network denial was configured but not independently exercised.
Overlapping denied-read/write paths can produce an ephemeral hidden mount: first write exit0 left host unchanged; separate protected-write fixture denied correctly.
Not a VM boundary or complete secret-isolation certification.
candidates.name: sandbox-runtime
candidates.role: Native filesystem/network restriction for selected commands

card_limitations: Open-source SDK license does not make hosted compute free or self-hostable.
modal run executes cloud code and may incur charges; not run here.
Do not assume native Codex subscription credentials belong in cloud containers.
candidates.name: modal
candidates.role: Managed elastic Python/GPU jobs and sandboxes

card_limitations: Accepted metrics ingestion/query, retained local storage and local rule/alert path only; no broker account, market-feed completeness or production availability claim.
Metrics are operational indicators, not an immutable transaction ledger or a subscription invoice.
Compare native final usage and completed-turn metrics; Codex transport startup prewarm can add token-bearing log events outside model-turn totals.
candidates.name: Prometheus
candidates.role: Metrics scraping, time-series retention and alert rules

card_limitations: Accepted local ingestion/query and receipt-specific storage retention/restart evidence only; no high-availability cluster or full transcript archive.
Loki indexes labels rather than all log content; sanitized logs cannot reconstruct removed prompt/tool payloads.
No tracing database or external telemetry destination was installed.
candidates.name: Loki
candidates.role: Retained local sanitized operational logs and LogQL queries

card_limitations: Import is not sandbox E2E.
Self-host guide targets AWS/GCP infrastructure; not a drop-in local Linux binary.
SDK, code-interpreter package and platform have separate versions.
candidates.name: e2b

card_limitations: Native acceptance covers 22 static public reference files and 160642 bytes at source commit 1d6c3d2f67aaef8e381193385360bb81b1b022d9; it excludes later integrations.
Repository, restore and password share one host. Host/volume loss, independent key recovery and off-host disaster recovery remain unproved.
No live SQLite/Qdrant/Loki/Prometheus database, native-client authentication store, transcript or broker/order journal was backed up.
Retention was dry-run only; no deletion/prune, backup schedule, external alerts or always-on hosting was enabled. Packed-byte reduction is not token savings.
candidates.name: Restic
candidates.role: Encrypted selected-file local backup and verified restore

card_limitations: No tracking server or experiment recorded by this task.
Autologging can capture requests and artifacts; enable selected integrations deliberately.
A registry score is not an out-of-sample financial guarantee.
candidates.name: mlflow
candidates.role: Versioned experiment artifacts, model lineage and optional traces

card_limitations: Accepted local message publication/retrieval and retained storage only; no delivery to a phone, email address or external topic.
The accepted webhook uses ntfy's native ?template=alertmanager integration; a plain arbitrary webhook endpoint is not equivalent.
No claim of guaranteed delivery, remote alerting or operational response coverage.
candidates.name: ntfy
candidates.role: Self-hosted local notification receipt and retrieval

card_limitations: ELv2 permits self-host use with restrictions; not Apache2 or unrestricted managed-service redistribution.
Server launch is prospective; no app instrumented and no judge-model calls run.
Auto-instrumentation can capture prompt/tool contents; scrub at source.

The proposed launch disables the optional MCP endpoint and hides built-in providers from the UI/catalog. PHOENIX_ALLOWED_PROVIDERS=NONE is not a backend inference authorization boundary; use a credential-free environment and appropriate access controls.
candidates.name: phoenix
candidates.role: Local trace inspection and evaluation workspace

card_limitations: Receipt proves the local alert path only; no external phone, email, Slack or paging destination was configured.
Alert deduplication does not provide broker-order idempotency or reconciliation.
No high-availability cluster or unattended remediation was accepted.
candidates.name: alertmanager
candidates.role: Local alert grouping, deduplication and routing

card_limitations: Native proof is through the contrib distribution using this core version; the standalone otelcol core binary was not separately exercised.
Collector delivery/redaction and native client task evidence are bounded by the receipt; no trace database, broker monitoring or external alert destination was accepted.
Local filter estimates and cache shares are not measured net provider savings; raw sessions remain outside public evidence.
candidates.name: opentelemetry-collector
candidates.role: OpenTelemetry core runtime used by the adopted contrib distribution

card_limitations: The binary release was published on 2026-09-16; the contrib source release was published on 2026-09-15. Neither date is the core source release date.
Accepted scope: native metrics/log delivery, sanitized canary and real Codex/Claude tasks; traces are disabled and no trace database was deployed.
Restart/retry and writer-identity details remain receipt-specific; this is not high availability or exact whole-account billing.
candidates.name: OpenTelemetry Collector contrib
candidates.role: Adopted native otelcol-contrib distribution and collection components

existing_overturn_when: Escalate to another scheduler, graph or host only when a specified long-running workflow, host-loss recovery, asset/backfill lineage or scale requirement exceeds the retained lane and the candidate passes the same failure, cancellation, output, identity and usage checks without duplicate effect owners.
limitations: Native worker success and telemetry matching are bounded by the recorded task, process and account. They do not establish every native client/session, whole-task savings or unlimited allowance.
Dagu's older completed-history restart is not in-flight recovery. Later recovery receipts must be evaluated for their own process, host and workload rather than promoting all workflows.
Gateway transport health, routed text and ACP research acceptance do not establish native hook/tool parity or independent provider/model attestation.
Same-host recovery and configured restrictions do not establish off-host disaster recovery, a VM boundary, unattended broker operation or paid hosting.
requirement: Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority.
requirement_note: The requirement, limitations and existing_overturn_when text is shared by this layer's group; judge fit against the layer title and layer_scope_terms.
rules: Judge from retained evidence. Open the evidence_refs of every adopted candidate (bounded: the referenced file or its relevant section) and record every path you opened in sources_read. Do not rely on memory of the repositories.

The winner set is 1-3 adopted candidates (adopted == true) that best satisfy the requirement on the evidence. why_selected must cite at least one evidence path and state what was actually observed (native execution, measured comparison, local integration, synthetic fixture or source review), not what the project claims.
Every adopted non-winner candidate appears in alternatives with a why_not_default that states the concrete evidence gap or trade-off; add non-adopted candidates only with the same standard.

If a non-adopted candidate would satisfy the requirement better on the evidence, do not select it: record it in challenger_preferred with the comparison (a fixtures/, blueprints/ or tests/ path, or a python3/node command) that would establish it. Agreement between lanes never promotes; only an executed comparison can.

overturn_when names the concrete check that would change the verdict (a fixtures/, blueprints/ or tests/ path or a runnable python3/node command). open_gaps lists what the evidence does not establish. limits lists what you could not read or verify. Do not invent paths, numbers or results; leave evidence_refs empty rather than guess.
title: Observability and hosting
